switch-from-stdio-to-http: Serve semantics: foreground/blocking by design (shell backgrounds: 'ai-raccoon serve > serve.log 2>&1 &'); detached daemon rejected (watchdog already solves the leak; honest URL needs the bound port).

stdout contract: serve owns stdout for the URI line or --mcp-entry JSON only; stderr carries everything else; --mcp-entry with a redirect must split streams (> entry.json 2> serve.log) or the JSON corrupts (R5).

Root launch options (--data-root/--install-scope/--transport) are PRE-VERB by System.CommandLine tree design: 'ai-raccoon serve --data-root X' errors with usage; correct form 'ai-raccoon --data-root X serve'. Consistent with all verbs; documented in help ('must precede the verb').

Attach probe: POST /mcp Accept 'application/json, text/event-stream' + non-JSON body -> recognized iff status in {400,405,406} AND body contains 'jsonrpc' (404 excluded: most common foreign answer). False-positive = another MCP/JSON-RPC server on the port; bounded + diagnosable via EventId 605 provenance. No stronger discriminator without a protocol addition (R15).

Watchdog: activity = ANY /mcp request (initialize/list/ping included) — an actively-connected client is 'in use'; guarantee is 'zero HTTP traffic for 4h', NOT 'no tool calls'. Background passes (extraction/watch/sync) never signal; only McpActivityMiddleware calls NotifyActivity (grep-gated).

integration-maintenance: The promotion queue was running TWO scorer generations at once: 204/288 rows carried v1 scores v3 could not reach, because a propose pass emitted only limit=20 deterministic candidates so rows ranked 21+ were never re-upserted. The default limit=50 review window was 100% v3 rows, which is why the sediment was invisible. Eviction ordered score ASC over the mixed column, so it deleted correctly-scored rows and preserved stale ones. Fix decouples the re-score set from the display limit.

A scope tier with few entries captured every scope=all search: the outer RRF scores by rank position alone, so a 1-entry tier's rank-1 and a 2400-entry tier's rank-1 both score weight/(k+1) and TIE, broken by ThenBy(Path, Ordinal). Max-normalization only inflated the displayed 1.0000 - it was not the cause. Fixed by fusing all contexts once against globally-ordered per-modality lists. Single-context parity exact (nDCG@5 0.674, MRR 0.881, sweep grids byte-identical). No measurement in the repo exercises scope=all with two populated tiers, so cross-context ranking quality still has no ground truth.

embedding-model-support: Manifest is the engine contract (ADR-0084): a local model directory carries ai-raccoon.manifest.json — dims, contextWindowTokens, tokenizer family+files, pooling mode, normalization, ONNX input/output names, per-file sha256 pins. A directory without one is REFUSED; a legacy `embedding.model=<path>.onnx` keeps the pre-manifest defaults. D7: the manifest's content IS the fingerprint, so re-downloading to the same path re-embeds.

Ordering is load-bearing in the migration drain: vec0 dimension reconcile is phase ONE, before the batch loop, in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE, create-if-missing-or-mismatch on BOTH vec_entries and vec_structure, no repopulate. Reconciling after the loop DROPs what the drain just wrote, with no pending rows left to re-drive it, so the migration finishes green over empty tables. (#432 later added a second call at server open for the serverless `model set` path — a matching dimension performs no DDL.)

Remote engines declare dims before anything is written: `model set openai --dims N` probes the endpoint pre-commit and refuses a contradicted value, silence on a non-384 endpoint, or an unreachable endpoint. Discovering it during the drain is too late — the bank is already pending behind a closed ToolGate (ADR-0076) with nothing able to finish it.

Fixtures derived from the implementation cannot falsify it — this recurred THREE times in one task. (1) modules.json names the Normalize module by index ('2', path '2_Normalize'), so matching on name wrote normalization:none for an L2-normalized model. (2) xlm-roberta declares neither add_bos_token nor add_eos_token — the behaviour lives in the tokenizer CLASS — so defaulting to false dropped the <s>…</s> wrapper. (3) #416: the sentencepiece test recorded bos=1 as 'NOT the xlm-roberta vocab ids, which differ' and then WEAKENED its assertion to 'two extra ids at the edges, whatever their values' instead of chasing it. All three produced working migrations with quietly wrong embeddings.

#416 (1.30.1): xlm-roberta numbers its vocabulary as the sentencepiece pieces shifted +1 behind fairseq's four specials (model vocab_size 250002 vs 250000 spm pieces). We fed raw spm ids, so the model read a neighbouring embedding row for EVERY token — deterministic, never crashing, semantically noise. Fixed by a manifest-declared tokenizer.options.vocabOffset (default 0, so T5/LLaMA are untouched), derived narrowly from tokenizer_class XLMRoberta*.

#423: #416 and #417 (derive special-token ids from the sp piece table) are each correct alone and unsafe together — the piece table numbers specials its own way, so an XLMRoberta* repo with no added_tokens_decoder would get sp-numbered specials alongside vocabOffset 1. Refused rather than derived from the fairseq convention, matching the ADR's posture toward guessing.

MEASURED OUTCOME, and it is negative: the vocab fix improved embedding geometry 4.4x (same-doc vs cross-doc cosine separation +0.0217 -> +0.0948, paired on 4,703 identical entries) but produced NO measurable retrieval change — paired per-query sign tests give p=0.10-0.16 across four arms, nothing significant either way. Fixed bge-m3 still loses to MiniLM by -0.233 nDCG@5 on eval-set-100 (p=0.001) and -0.539 on test-set-10 (p=0.008).

Two methodological traps this cost. (a) Absolute cosine separation is NOT comparable across models — bge-m3 sits at a 0.50 random-pair baseline vs MiniLM's 0.25, so a smaller absolute gap is not less information; that invalid comparison was used as evidence of a further defect after the reason it is invalid had already been written down. (b) A large M2 gain (M2 up-weights ftsWeight over vectorWeight) means a WEAKER vector leg, which is equally consistent with 'wrong model for this corpus' as with 'broken' — a hint, not proof.

Verified correct, do NOT re-investigate: pooling (CLS-over-token_embeddings equals the graph's own sentence_embedding at cosine 1.00000000, maxAbsDiff 1.5e-8 — #435 closed not-a-defect) and tokenization (id-for-id against HuggingFace's XLMRobertaTokenizer rule computed from the real sentencepiece.bpe.model, incl. CJK, accents, em dash, snake_case).

Still open: bge-m3's loss is most likely suitability, untested — this corpus is short English chunks cut to a 256-token budget, all-MiniLM-L6-v2's trained sweet spot and the opposite of bge-m3's design (multilingual, 8192-token). A fair test needs the corpus re-chunked at the engine's own budget, which pairs naturally with the OQ5 eval repos. M2 transferability is therefore UNANSWERED (M2's gain on MiniLM is itself not significant, p=0.265).

G3 golden-vector gate is architecture-local: the bundled model is qint8 and x64/ARM requantise differently (measured cosine 0.9895 between captures). CI enforces token-id equality (exact, arch-independent) plus a coarse 0.95 breakage floor; the tight bound holds only on the capture arch. Restoring it on CI needs a per-architecture capture.

Operational traps worth keeping: `serve` self-terminates after 4h without MCP activity and a drain generates none (use --idle-timeout 0); a bank copied from the live bank inherits its watch rows and keeps re-ingesting real directories mid-experiment (DELETE FROM watches first); `model set` with no --port dials 7721, the user's live server; vec0 tables cannot be touched from the plain sqlite3 CLI, so pruning a bank copy either fails on the vec_structure_ad trigger or leaves orphaned vector rows that silently occupy result slots.

KEY PITFALLS LEARNED: (1) --nologo is VSTest-only; under MTP dotnet test forwards it and reports 'Zero tests ran / exit 5' (dotnet/sdk#55309) — drop it from every dotnet test invocation. (2) MTP drops xunit MESSAGE-BUS DiagnosticMessages — xRetry's per-attempt 'attempt (1/N)' lines are invisible under MTP in every flag combo (--xunit-diagnostics on / --xunit-internal-diagnostics on / -v n / --diagnostic file); only diagnostic-SINK messages (TestContext.SendDiagnosticMessage) surface. Retry visibility = permanent probes + exhaustion still red with last-attempt exception. (3) An attribute-rename swap can silently break TEXT-SCANNING gates (EnvGateReaderRuleTests matched literal '[Fact]'; scan set 13->2) — sweep for gates matching attribute literals before swapping. (4) Retry fixtures: xRetry re-runs the failed method inside the same test-case execution; class/collection fixtures are NOT re-created per attempt — failed-attempt side effects persist into the retry. (5) xunit 4.0.0: [CollectionDefinition(DisableParallelization=true)] is NOT obsolete (only assembly-level CollectionBehavior props are); xUnit1069 (Timeout without TestContext.Current.CancellationToken) is a new analyzer; RetryFactAttribute derives FactAttribute (Skip inherited). (6) xRetry.v3 1.0.0 pins xunit.v3.extensibility.core [4.0.0,5.0.0) — built for 4.0.0; xRetry.v3.Reqnroll 1.0.0 exists for BDD retry.
